intent: Trace the maximum long-term capital gains tax rate from 1960 through 2021 and compare the current rate with the proposed rate for high earners.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
What is the long-term trend of the maximum long-term capital gains tax rate from 1960 through 2021?
How does the current maximum long-term capital gains tax rate compare with the proposed rate for high earners?

units.claim: All 2 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The maximum long-term capital gains tax rate fluctuated over 1960–2021, starting at 25% in 1960, peaking at 35% from 1972 through 1977, falling to 15% from 2003 through 2012, and ending at 20% in 2021.
units.computation: Trace the series from 1960 to 2021: start 25%; maximum 35% across 1972–1977; minimum 15% across 2003–2012; end 20% in 2021.
accept: Rate starts at 25% in 1960 and ends at 20% in 2021.
Rate reaches a low of 15% from 2003 through 2012.
Overall the rate fluctuates rather than moving monotonically.
reject: Rate is constant over the period.
Rate ends higher than it started.

units.claim: The current maximum long-term capital gains tax rate in 2021 is 20%, while the proposed rate for high earners is 39.6% in 2022, so the proposed rate is 19.6 percentage points higher (nearly double).
units.computation: Compare current 2021 rate (20%) with proposed 2022 rate (39.6%); difference = 39.6 − 20 = 19.6 percentage points; ratio = 39.6 / 20 = 1.98.
accept: Proposed rate exceeds current rate by 19.6 percentage points.
Proposed rate is approximately double the current rate.
reject: Current and proposed rates are equal.
Proposed rate is lower than current rate.
Difference is stated as 39.6 percentage points.

optional_valid: Mention that the proposed series has only two points (2021 anchor at 20% and 2022 estimate at 39.6%).
unsupported_to_avoid: Claims about other tax brackets or earners not shown.
review_notes: The proposed series includes a 2021 anchor equal to the current rate and a 2022 estimate; the comparison unit uses the 2022 proposed value against the 2021 current value as requested.
Trend unit summarizes the full 1960–2021 path without enumerating every data point.
Closure truth correction 2026-10-29: claims, ranges, computations, and relations were checked against data_table.csv.
